Information since December indicates continued labor-market strengthening and solid real activity, with gains in employment, household spending, and business fixed investment. This pattern aligns with financial-accelerator mechanisms in which stronger balance sheets lower external finance premia and support investment, and with New Keynesian dynamics linking reduced slack and higher real marginal costs to a gradual firming of inflation toward the symmetric 2 percent objective. Holding the federal funds rate at 1.25–1.50 percent while signaling gradual increases is consistent with estimated Taylor-type policy rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and with a floor-style operating framework using interest on reserves and ON RRPs (Goodfriend, 2002). Market-based inflation compensation has risen but remains low, consistent with term-structure evidence that macro factors shape expected inflation and the term premium (Ang and Piazzesi, 2003; Rudebusch and Wu, 2008).
